textFacts.fact: Theorem 43: two oppositely directed rays are centrally symmetric about the midpoint of the segment joining their starting points.
The proof considers non-collinear, oppositely directed rays AB and A_1B_1; O is the midpoint of AA_1.
Central symmetry with center O sends A to A_1, supporting line AB to parallel supporting line A_1B_1, half-plane alpha to alpha_1, and ray AB onto ray A_1B_1.

textFacts.locator: lesson.json /prose/19 and /prose/20; source_refs p0164#1 and p0164#2
textFacts.fact: The coincident-support case is proved similarly; centrally symmetric rays are oppositely directed. The original fig-217 displays the distinct-support case, not a second collinear panel.
For rays on distinct parallel lines, the line joining starting points divides the plane; the two ray interiors lie in opposite half-planes when directions are opposite.

sourceRequirements.fact: One shared frame; no separated panels. Preserve all five labelled point roles and both region-label occurrences.
Boundary incidence and strict order P217-02, P217-03, P217-04; the boundary continues beyond both origins.
The center is the midpoint of the two origins.
Each labelled direction point belongs to its own ray; the two supports are distinct and parallel, and the ray directions are opposite.
The ray interiors are on opposite open sides of the same boundary; both origins and the center are on the boundary, not inside a half-plane.

An exact centrally symmetric defining realization must pair both ray origins and both chosen corresponding ray samples about the same center. An origin-only assertion does not cover the sample points.
sourceRequirements.metricQualification: The raw proof maps whole rays but does not separately assert that the printed symbols B and B_1 name mutually symmetric measured points. Pairing chosen defining samples is an exact mathematical realization requirement, not a measurement extracted from ink.

sourceRequirements.fact: The boundary line is invariant as a set under the half-turn; the two supporting lines and the two half-planes exchange.
Retain a distinguishable upper and lower half-plane and each region token. Only the lower displayed region is hatched; the entire decorated raster is not being claimed centrally symmetric.

Both meaningful ray connections and all three boundary incidences must survive. Do not replace the two rays with unrelated segments, omit either direction sample, or add an unshown second proof panel.

completeCenterSymmetryLedger.additionalFiniteGeometryRule: If a future candidate claims half-turn equality for finite ray truncations or other added vertices, include their corresponding opposite pairs too. Original clipping endpoints and hatch endpoints are not extra named mathematical points.
completeCenterSymmetryLedger.noUnsupportedSymmetryClaim: One-sided hatching, label typography and image clipping are not invariant decorated objects; do not demand symmetry of those decorations or use them as distance data.

independentSolution.fact: The half-turn sends the first origin to the second, its support to the unique parallel through the second origin, and the open side containing the first ray to the opposite open side. The second origin, transformed support and opposite side uniquely determine the second ray.

sourceRequirements.fact: All eight point roles and label occurrences belong to one frame with exactly three displayed supports. Do not split the intersections into unrelated panels.
Upper support strict left-to-right order is P218-01, P218-02, P218-03.
Lower support strict left-to-right order is P218-04, P218-05, P218-06.
Diagonal strict lower-left-to-upper-right order is P218-07, P218-05, P218-02, P218-08. Both exterior diagonal points and the interval between intersections are indispensable.
The two distinct horizontal supports realize the text's parallel-support pair. The choice of printed endpoint glyph identities is not established here.
A single nonparallel diagonal crosses both horizontals exactly at the two shared intersection roles; retain all seven consecutive connections in the connection ledger.

The same/opposite-direction solution depends on all three support orders, including the diagonal. Do not invent connections between off-support points or print solution-class arrows as source content.

independentSolution.notation: [P218-i,P218-j) is the ray beginning at the first source point and passing through the second. These are token-based reviewer relations, not a disclosed answer key or proposed visible labels.
independentSolution.derivationRule: On each ordered support, first-to-later rays share the forward direction and later-to-first rays share the backward direction. The two horizontal supports are parallel, so combine their forward classes and combine their backward classes. The diagonal has its own two classes.
independentSolution.crossFamilyRelation: No horizontal ray is same-direction or opposite-direction to a diagonal ray because their supports are nonparallel.
independentSolution.enumerationScope: All ray names obtainable from distinct labelled point roles on a displayed support. This is not a claim that 24 arrowed rays were separately printed.
independentSolution.textRoleTransport: Text fixes names AB and CD for the parallel pair. Printed endpoint identities, intersection identities and diagonal endpoint identities remain UNKNOWN; no Latin/Cyrillic or other character map is guessed.
